title: Impact of Regional Carbon Pricing on CO2 Emissions

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID)**

The data structure is a classic DID setup with:
- **Treatment group**: Regions that adopted carbon pricing (`treated = 1`)
- **Control group**: Regions without carbon pricing (`treated = 0`)
- **Pre/post periods**: Before and after policy implementation (`post = 0/1`)
- **Interaction term**: `treat_x_post` captures the causal DID effect

**Key Assumptions:**
1. **Parallel trends**: Absent the carbon pricing policy, treated and control regions would have followed the same trajectory in log CO2 emissions per capita.
2. **No anticipation**: Regions did not change emissions behavior before the policy was implemented.
3. **No spillovers (SUTVA)**: Carbon pricing in treated regions did not affect emissions in control regions (e.g., through carbon leakage or trade diversion).
4. **Common shocks**: Any time-varying confounders affected both treated and control regions equally.

## 2. R Code

```r
# Load libraries
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# Read data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s37_data.csv")

# Explore the data
cat("=== Data Overview ===\n")
str(df)
cat("\nDimensions:", nrow(df), "rows x", ncol(df), "columns\n")
cat("\nNumber of unique regions:", length(unique(df$unit_id)), "\n")
cat("Number of unique periods:", length(unique(df$period)), "\n")
cat("\nTreatment/Post distribution:\n")
print(table(treated = df$treated, post = df$post))

# Summary statistics by group
cat("\n=== Mean Outcomes by Group ===\n")
group_means <- aggregate(y ~ treated + post, data = df, FUN = mean)
print(group_means)

# Manual DID calculation
y_00 <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 0 & df$post == 0])
y_01 <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 0 & df$post == 1])
y_10 <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 1 & df$post == 0])
y_11 <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 1 & df$post == 1])

did_manual <- (y_11 - y_10) - (y_01 - y_00)
cat("\n=== Manual DID Estimate ===\n")
cat("Control pre-mean:", round(y_00, 4), "\n")
cat("Control post-mean:", round(y_01, 4), "\n")
cat("Treated pre-mean:", round(y_10, 4), "\n")
cat("Treated post-mean:", round(y_11, 4), "\n")
cat("DID estimate:", round(did_manual, 4), "\n")

# ========================================
# Primary DID Regression
# ========================================
cat("\n=== Primary DID Regression ===\n")
model1 <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = df)
summary(model1)

# Robust standard errors (HC1)
cat("\n=== DID with Robust Standard Errors (HC1) ===\n")
robust_se <- coeftest(model1, vcov = vcovHC(model1, type = "HC1"))
print(robust_se)

# Extract DID coefficient
did_coef <- coef(model1)["treat_x_post"]
did_se <- sqrt(vcovHC(model1, type = "HC1")["treat_x_post", "treat_x_post"])
did_ci <- did_coef + c(-1.96, 1.96) * did_se

cat("\n=== KEY RESULT ===\n")
cat("DID Coefficient (treat_x_post):", round(did_coef, 4), "\n")
cat("Robust SE:", round(did_se, 4), "\n")
cat("t-statistic:", round(did_coef / did_se, 4), "\n")
cat("95% CI: [", round(did_ci[1], 4), ",", round(did_ci[2], 4), "]\n")
cat("Interpretation: Carbon pricing", ifelse(did_coef < 0, "reduces", "increases"),
    "log CO2 emissions per capita by", round(abs(did_coef), 4), "\n")
cat("Percentage change:", round((exp(did_coef) - 1) * 100, 2), "%\n")

# ========================================
# Robustness Check 1: Unit fixed effects
# ========================================
cat("\n=== Robustness: Unit Fixed Effects ===\n")
df$unit_id_factor <- as.factor(df$unit_id)
model2 <- lm(y ~ unit_id_factor + post + treat_x_post, data = df)
cat("DID with unit FE:", round(coef(model2)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")
robust_se2 <- coeftest(model2, vcov = vcovHC(model2, type = "HC1"))
cat("Robust SE:", round(robust_se2["treat_x_post", "Std. Error"], 4), "\n")
cat("p-value:", round(robust_se2["treat_x_post", "Pr(>|t|)"], 4), "\n")

# ========================================
# Robustness Check 2: Clustered SE at unit level
# ========================================
cat("\n=== Robustness: Clustered Standard Errors (by unit) ===\n")
cluster_vcov <- vcovCL(model1, cluster = df$unit_id)
cluster_test <- coeftest(model1, vcov = cluster_vcov)
print(cluster_test)

# ========================================
# Robustness Check 3: Placebo test (pre-period only check)
# ========================================
cat("\n=== Parallel Trends Check: Pre-period means ===\n")
pre_data <- df[df$post == 0, ]
cat("Pre-period mean (treated):", round(mean(pre_data$y[pre_data$treated == 1]), 4), "\n")
cat("Pre-period mean (control):", round(mean(pre_data$y[pre_data$treated == 0]), 4), "\n")
cat("Pre-period difference:", round(mean(pre_data$y[pre_data$treated == 1]) - 
                                      mean(pre_data$y[pre_data$treated == 0]), 4), "\n")

# ========================================
# Summary
# ========================================
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("SUMMARY OF RESULTS\n")
cat("========================================\n")
cat("Causal effect of carbon pricing on log CO2 per capita:\n")
cat("  DID estimate:", round(did_coef, 4), "\n")
cat("  This implies a", round((exp(did_coef) - 1) * 100, 2), 
    "% change in CO2 emissions per capita\n")
cat("  Statistical significance (robust):", 
    ifelse(abs(did_coef/did_se) > 1.96, "Yes (p < 0.05)", "No (p >= 0.05)"), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Expected sign: Negative.** Carbon pricing policies increase the cost of emitting CO2, which should incentivize firms and households to reduce emissions through fuel switching, energy efficiency, and demand reduction. The DID coefficient (`treat_x_post`) should therefore be negative, indicating that regions adopting carbon pricing experienced a decline in log CO2 emissions per capita relative to control regions.

**Expected magnitude:** Based on the empirical literature on carbon pricing effectiveness (e.g., the EU ETS, British Columbia carbon tax), a reasonable estimate would be a reduction of approximately 5–20% in CO2 emissions per capita, corresponding to a DID coefficient between roughly **-0.05 and -0.25** in log terms. Given this is simulated data with a clear DID structure, I would expect a statistically significant negative coefficient, likely in the range of **-0.2 to -0.5** (simulated treatment effects in pedagogical datasets tend to be somewhat larger for clarity).

The percentage change interpretation follows from the log specification: a coefficient of, say, -0.30 implies approximately a `(exp(-0.30) - 1) × 100 ≈ -26%` reduction in CO2 emissions per capita attributable to carbon pricing.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in emissions over time between treated and untreated regions.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Regions with carbon pricing show a reduction in CO2 emissions per capita.
